q01.key_idea: Count every circle, big and small, one group at a time.
steps: The 2 blue ears are circles, and each ear has a green circle inside: 2 + 2 = 4.
The big face is 1 more circle: 4 + 1 = 5.
The 2 orange eyes and the purple mouth are circles too: 5 + 3 = 8.

choice_feedback.A: You may have missed the small circles inside the ears or the face.
choice_feedback.B: You may have missed the green circles inside the ears.
choice_feedback.C: You may have missed one circle. Count the eyes, the mouth and the inner ear circles.
choice_feedback.E: You may have counted one circle twice.

q02.key_idea: Each round shape seen from the top is a round block, and each square or rectangle is a block with flat sides.
steps: From the top we see a blue rectangle under everything. So the bottom block is a blue box.
On the left is a plain yellow circle. That can be a yellow cone standing on the box.
On the right is a white square inside a red circle. That is a white cube on a red round block.
Picture A shows a yellow cone and a white cube on a red round block, all on a blue box.

choice_feedback.B: The bottom block here is red and round, but from the top the bottom is a blue rectangle.
choice_feedback.C: The red block here is a cube, but from the top the red part is round.
choice_feedback.D: The yellow block here is a cube, but from the top the yellow shape is a circle.
choice_feedback.E: The bottom block here is round, but from the top the bottom is a rectangle.

q03.key_idea: Find half of 24, then see how many coloured squares are missing.
steps: Count the coloured squares row by row: 4 + 1 + 1 + 3 = 9.
Half of 24 squares is 12.
12 - 9 = 3 more squares need to be coloured.

choice_feedback.A: With 1 more there are 10 coloured squares, not 12.
choice_feedback.B: With 2 more there are 11 coloured squares, not 12.
choice_feedback.D: With 4 more there are 13 coloured squares, more than half.
choice_feedback.E: With 5 more there are 14 coloured squares, more than half.

q04.key_idea: When the disc spins, the two holes always stay the same number of hours apart.
steps: In the picture the holes show 1 and 5.
Going round the clock from 1 to 5 is 4 steps: 2, 3, 4, 5.
So the two holes must always be 4 steps apart.
Picture D shows 3 and 7. From 3 to 7 is 4 steps: 4, 5, 6, 7.

choice_feedback.E: From 5 to 7 is only 2 steps, not 4.

q05.key_idea: Find each piece of the square inside the kangaroo, and see which piece is left over.
steps: The square on the left is cut into 7 pieces: 2 big triangles, 1 middle triangle, 2 small triangles, 1 square and 1 slanted piece.
In the kangaroo, the 2 small triangles are the ear and the arm, and the 2 big triangles make the body.
The square is in the leg, and the middle triangle is the foot.
The slanted piece with 4 sides is nowhere in the kangaroo.

choice_feedback.B: This small triangle is used in the kangaroo.
choice_feedback.C: The square is used in the kangaroo's leg.
choice_feedback.D: This small triangle is used in the kangaroo.
choice_feedback.E: This middle triangle is used as the kangaroo's foot.

q06.key_idea: The road crosses itself at every red dot, so Steven drives through each red dot two times.
steps: Count the red dots: there are 7.
Follow the road from X with your finger. At each red dot the road crosses another part of itself.
So your finger goes through every red dot two times: once on each part of the road.
7 + 7 = 14 stops.

choice_feedback.A: 11 is too few. Steven goes through each of the 7 red dots two times.
choice_feedback.B: 12 is too few. Steven goes through each of the 7 red dots two times.
choice_feedback.C: 13 is 1 too few. Check that you counted both visits at every red dot.
choice_feedback.E: 15 is 1 too many. There are 7 red dots and each one is passed two times.

q07.key_idea: A tree that is closer can hide a tree that is behind it.
steps: Stand at D and look toward the trees. The 2 big trees are closest to D.
The top big tree is right in front of the 2 small trees at the top, so they are hidden.
The bottom big tree is right in front of the small tree at the bottom left, so it is hidden too.
So from D the beaver sees only the 2 big trees whole.

choice_feedback.A: From A, more than 2 trees can be seen whole.
choice_feedback.B: From B, more than 2 trees can be seen whole.
choice_feedback.C: From C, more than 2 trees can be seen whole.
choice_feedback.E: From E, more than 2 trees can be seen whole.

q08.key_idea: Check both rules for each boat: more than 1 circle, and 2 more triangles than squares.
steps: Boat C has only 1 circle, so it is out.
Count triangles and squares on the other boats.
Boat E has 3 circles, 4 triangles and 2 squares.
4 is 2 more than 2, so boat E follows both rules.

choice_feedback.A: Boat A has 2 triangles and 1 square. That is only 1 more triangle.
choice_feedback.B: Boat B has 3 triangles and 2 squares. That is only 1 more triangle.
choice_feedback.D: Boat D has fewer triangles than squares.

q09.key_idea: Walk straight until a wall is in front of you, then turn right.
steps: From START Robbie goes up to a wall and turns right. Then he goes down a little and turns right to walk left. Then he turns right and goes up all the way to the top.
At the top he turns right, goes to the right wall, and turns right to go down. He passes D, because it is beside him, not in front of him.
He hits a block, turns right and walks left along the long middle row to the left wall. He turns right, goes up to the top, turns right, and soon meets a wall again.
He turns right and goes down to the big block at the bottom. He turns right, walks left, and goes out at A.

choice_feedback.B: Robbie goes past the B opening on his side and then turns away from it.
choice_feedback.C: Robbie goes past the C opening on his side. A wall is in front of him only later.
choice_feedback.D: Robbie goes past D on his side. He only turns when a wall is in front of him.
choice_feedback.E: Robbie never walks toward E. He is facing the other way when he is near it.

q10.key_idea: Both question tokens are the same, so take away the known numbers and split what is left in half.
steps: 10 + 2 = 12, and 18 - 12 = 6. So the two question tokens add up to 6.
The two tokens are the same: 3 + 3 = 6. Each one is 3.

q11.key_idea: After unfolding, every hole has a twin on the other side of the fold, like in a mirror.
steps: The fold is the dashed line on the right of the folded paper. After unfolding, it is the line in the middle.
The circle is at the top, far from the fold. So there are 2 circles at the top, near the outside edges.
The square is at the bottom, right next to the fold. So there are 2 squares at the bottom, next to the middle line.
Picture B shows this.

choice_feedback.A: The 2 sides are not mirror images: one circle is near the middle line and the other is near the edge.
choice_feedback.C: Here a circle faces a square. Each hole's twin must be the same shape.
choice_feedback.D: The squares here are as far from the middle line as the circles, but they should be right next to it.
choice_feedback.E: Here the squares are near the edges and the circles near the middle. It should be the other way round.

q12.key_idea: Find how many apples came out in all, then share that equally among the 3 bags.
steps: The bags now have 3 + 4 + 6 = 13 apples.
Maria had 19, so she took out 19 - 13 = 6 apples.
She took the same number from each of the 3 bags: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6. So 2 from each bag.

choice_feedback.A: Taking 1 from each bag takes out 3 apples. Then 16 would be left, not 13.
choice_feedback.C: Taking 3 from each bag takes out 9 apples. Then only 10 would be left, not 13.
choice_feedback.D: Taking 4 from each bag takes out 12 apples. Then only 7 would be left, not 13.
choice_feedback.E: Taking 5 from each bag takes out 15 apples. Then only 4 would be left, not 13.

q13.key_idea: Going around the ring, add the roads both ways and see where the two totals match.
steps: The roads are A to B 7, B to C 2, C to D 6, D to E 4, and E to A 5.
From B to E one way, through A: 7 + 5 = 12.
From B to E the other way, through C and D: 2 + 6 + 4 = 12.
Both ways are 12, so B and E are the same distance apart either way.

choice_feedback.B: From B to D: 2 + 6 = 8 one way, but 7 + 5 + 4 = 16 the other way.
choice_feedback.C: From C to E: 6 + 4 = 10 one way, but 2 + 7 + 5 = 14 the other way.
choice_feedback.D: From A to C: 7 + 2 = 9 one way, but 5 + 4 + 6 = 15 the other way.
choice_feedback.E: From A to D: 5 + 4 = 9 one way, but 7 + 2 + 6 = 15 the other way.

q14.key_idea: Find Sam's only path through each floor, and use the stairs to go between them.
steps: On floor 1 Sam comes in at the front right and walks to the stairs at the front left. She sees no sticker there.
She goes up. On floor 2 she must reach the stairs at the back right. On the way she passes the shark first, and later the rhino.
She goes down the back stairs to floor 1. She walks along the back row past the frog and out.
The order is shark, rhino, frog.

choice_feedback.A: The frog is in the back row of floor 1, and Sam only gets there at the very end.
choice_feedback.C: On floor 2 Sam reaches the shark before the rhino.
choice_feedback.D: The frog comes last, after Sam comes back down from floor 2.
choice_feedback.E: Sam passes both animals on floor 2 before she comes down to the frog.

q15.key_idea: Check each minute and see if the green, red and blue bars are all on.
steps: At minute 8, the green, red and blue bars are all on.
At minutes 12 and 13, all three bars are on again.
At every other minute at least one light is off. So all three are on for 3 minutes.

choice_feedback.A: Some of those minutes have one light off. Check each bar minute by minute.
choice_feedback.B: Check minutes 7, 9 and 11 again: one light is off in each of them.
choice_feedback.D: You may have missed one of minutes 8, 12 and 13.
choice_feedback.E: All three lights are on at more than 1 minute: 8, 12 and 13.

q16.key_idea: Line up the dancers from first to last and count them.
steps: Emma is third, so 2 dancers finished ahead of her.
After Emma come 3 dancers, and then the last dancer.
2 + 1 + 3 + 1 = 7 dancers.

choice_feedback.A: Only 4 dancers would leave no room for 3 dancers between Emma and last place.
choice_feedback.B: With 5 dancers, there is only 1 dancer between Emma and last place.
choice_feedback.C: With 6 dancers, there are only 2 dancers between Emma and last place.
choice_feedback.E: With 8 dancers, there are 4 dancers between Emma and last place.

q17.key_idea: Each piece fits on the grid in only one way, so add up the numbers each piece covers.
steps: The grid is 1, 4, 7 on top, 9, 5, 6 in the middle and 2, 8, 3 at the bottom.
Piece A covers 2 + 8 + 3 + 6 + 7 = 26. Piece B covers 2 + 8 + 5 + 6 + 7 = 28.
Piece C covers 4 + 9 + 5 + 6 + 8 = 32. Piece D covers 1 + 4 + 5 + 8 + 3 = 21.
Piece E covers 4 + 7 + 9 + 5 + 8 = 33. That is the biggest sum.

choice_feedback.C: Piece C covers 32, just 1 less than 33.
choice_feedback.D: Piece D covers 21, the smallest sum.

q18.key_idea: List every way to place the cards, then count only the sums that are different.
steps: The different sums are 13, 14, 15, 22, 24, 32 and 33. That is 7.

choice_feedback.A: 6 is 1 too few. Check the list again: 13, 14, 15, 22, 24, 32, 33.
choice_feedback.C: 8 is too many. Some ways give the same sum, like 12 + 1 and 11 + 2.
choice_feedback.D: 10 is too many. Some ways give the same sum, so count each sum once.
choice_feedback.E: 12 is how many ways there are to place the cards. Some of them give the same sum.
